chunks.text: Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) is a species in the mulberry family Moraceae, first formally described by Jean-Baptiste Lamarck in 1789; its English name comes from Portuguese 'jaca,' which in turn traces back to the Malayalam word 'chakka.' It originated in the Western Ghats of India and has since spread through South and Southeast Asia, Africa, the Americas and Oceania, thriving in tropical lowlands below about 1,600 metres in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil; as of 2024 India is the leading producer, at about 1.436 million tonnes, ahead of Bangladesh, Thailand and Indonesia. The tree is evergreen and can reach 30 metres tall. Its fruit is the largest tree-borne fruit in the world, measuring 20-90 cm long and up to 15-50 cm wide and weighing as much as 50 kilograms; the thick, tubercled rind turns from green to brownish-yellow as it ripens, and inside are 100-500 sweet, fleshy yellow bulbs, each wrapped around a single seed. Jackfruit has been cultivated in India for an estimated 3,000-6,000 years, and a tree can keep fruiting for over a century after first bearing fruit at 4-14 years old.

Ripe jackfruit bulbs taste faintly of pineapple or banana and are eaten fresh or turned into jams, candies and drinks, while unripe (raw) jackfruit is cooked in curries across South and Southeast Asia, often with coconut milk, and has become popular internationally as a meat substitute for its fibrous texture. The seeds can be boiled, roasted, or ground into flour, and roasted seeds have even been explored as a cocoa substitute. In traditional medicine, different parts of the tree have been used variously: roots for fever and asthma, leaves as an antiseptic for wounds, bark as an anaesthetic, and sap mixed with vinegar as a folk snakebite remedy. The termite- and fungus-resistant timber is prized for furniture and construction and is the traditional wood used for the Indian veena and other musical instruments, as well as for Buddhist statuary; monastic robes have historically been dyed using jackfruit wood extract. Jackfruit is the national fruit of Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, and the state fruit of Kerala and Tamil Nadu in India; roughly 75% of harvested fruit is estimated to spoil because of its short shelf life.
